core_obligations: Reduce to an injective sheaf (proof lines 18487-18495): fix a prime ell and let I be injective on X; then f_*I is injective on Y, which is the input needed to apply the base change hypothesis for g.

Set up the base change square (proof lines 18497-18504): for Z' -> Z put Y' = Z' x_Z Y and X' = Z' x_Z X = Y' x_Y X with projections a, b, c and base-changed f', g'; the pushforward base change formula gives b^{-1}f_*I = f'_*a^{-1}I.

Apply the hypotheses (proof lines 18505-18510): the hypothesis on f gives R^q f'_*a^{-1}I = 0 for q > 0, and the hypothesis on g applied to the injective sheaf f_*I gives R^q g'_*b^{-1}f_*I = 0 for q > 0.

Conclude by Leray (proof lines 18511-18516): in the relative Leray spectral sequence R^p g'_* R^q f'_* a^{-1}I => R^{p+q}(g' o f')_*a^{-1}I all entries with q > 0 vanish, so R^p(g' o f')_*a^{-1}I = 0 for p > 0, which is the base change property for the composite.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to injective torsion sheaves and use that f_* of an injective sheaf is injective.
Pull back the composite base change square and apply the two hypotheses to the terms of the relative Leray spectral sequence.
Degenerate the spectral sequence to obtain the vanishing for the composite.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that base change for proper morphisms is stable under composition (statement lines 18476-18484). The proof (proof lines 18486-18516) reduces to an injective torsion sheaf I, uses that f_*I is again injective so that the hypothesis on g applies, and then degenerates the relative Leray spectral sequence for the base-changed composite, whose two families of inputs vanish by the two hypotheses. H2: one reduction plus one spectral-sequence degeneration, written out.
